en.title: D
en.summary: The letter name is De, as in the word Danke.

sections.title: The letter De
paragraphs: German names this letter (De) /deː/. Its main sound is heard in (Danke) /ˈdaŋkə/, which means thank you. This letter makes two different sounds in German.

sections.title: How to say De
paragraphs: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Release the air while vibrating your vocal cords. Touch the same spot behind your upper teeth for the second sound. Release the air sharply without voice. Place a hand on your throat to feel the voice stop.

sections.title: Spelling rules for De
paragraphs: This letter makes the voiced sound /d/ at the beginning of a word or syllable. You hear this sound in (oder) /ˈoːdɐ/. It changes to the crisp sound /t/ at the end of a syllable or word. You hear this voiceless sound in (Bad) /baːt/ and in (und) /ʊnt/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with De
paragraphs: Do not voice the final sound like the end of bed. Stop your vocal cords and say a clean sound like the end of bet.
